correctness.rationale: For every b,k≥2 write k=2^s t (t odd), U=(b^t−1)/(b−1), H=(b^k−1)/(b^t−1). Fixed-width leading block coefficients include consecutive integers (or 1), so gcd reduces to gcd of R_{b,k}(h). For odd h each b^(2^i t)+1 divides b^(2^i t h)+1, giving H; KSS unrestricted gcd for the odd t-part supplies gcd(t,U). Since U is odd, H≡2^s (mod U) is a unit, and widths 1,t give the matching upper bound. For t=1 the coincident witness is handled separately. Even widths reduce exactly to base b² KSS. The independent exact-integer diagnostic passed 161 (b,k) pairs with all necessary witness widths; earlier fixed bounded-width tester was corrected, not used to draw mathematical conclusions.

evidence: Kane–Sanna–Shallit Theorem 1 determines gcd_{h≥1} R_{b,k}(h) and its Waring-type extension; for odd k its 1,k witnesses already settle the odd widths. Their base b² substitution settles even widths. Their theorem does not supply the even-k odd-width higher gcd as stated.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The bigger unrestricted class has a smaller gcd; a theorem about that gcd does not imply the exact restricted gcd. b=2,k=4 yields unrestricted 1 but odd-width 15. No stronger exact odd-only theorem found.

originality.rationale: Kane–Sanna–Shallit Theorem 1 determines unrestricted-width gcd and gives two witnesses at widths 1,k. It already implies the odd-k odd-width result and the even-width b² result, both credited as prior. value.rationale: The gcd of k-fold repeated digit blocks is a natural additive congruence invariant. Restricting block width to odd values, for even k, changes it by an arbitrarily large factor; exact closed form plus two specific witness widths gives a reusable arithmetic obstruction for parity-constrained digit powers. This is not an arbitrary slice or just the base-four corollary; those preexisting branches are expressly excluded from the originality claim.
